Small Batch Cold Brew For One

You do not need a gallon jar to make cold brew at home. A single pint jar with 40g of coarse grounds and 320ml of cold water gives you two strong glasses the next morning. Stir once, cover the jar, and leave it on the counter for 14 hours before straining through a paper filter.

The pint method is also the cheapest way to test a new bag of beans before committing a full batch to it. If the small jar tastes muddy, adjust the grind coarser rather than cutting the steep short, because a short steep loses the body that makes cold brew worth drinking.

Strain slowly and never press the grounds, pressing pushes fine particles through the filter and the silt keeps extracting in the fridge, turning the second glass bitter by the time you pour it. Serve over ice, cut with water or milk to taste, and drink it within four days.
